ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening of all UBOs, directors, and authorized signatories against the United Nations Security Council Consolidated List, OFAC Specially Designated Nationals (SDN) List, EU Consolidated Financial Sanctions List, and the Korean Financial Intelligence Unit (KoFIU) domestic sanctions list. Additionally, conduct enhanced due diligence for Politically Exposed Persons (PEPs) as defined by the Financial Action Task Force (FATF) and the Korean AML Act, including family members and close associates. Screening must be performed at onboarding and continuously updated on a real-time basis using automated systems. Any positive match triggers immediate suspension of the incorporation process and mandatory reporting to KoFIU within 24 hours. The protocol must also include adverse media checks and verification of source of funds for any high-risk jurisdictions.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Commercial Act of the Republic of Korea, Act No. 1000 as amended; specifically Articles 169, 287, 287-2, 287-3, 287-4, 287-5, 287-6, 287-7, 287-12, 290, 292, 543, 545, and 546 concerning establishment of a Yuhan Hoesa (limited liability company), member capital subscription, articles of incorporation, registration, representation, and dissolution-related governance.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Registration Division of the District Court under the Supreme Court of Korea; online administrative access through the Saeol e-Registration Portal and coordinated business registration through the National Tax Service Hometax system.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Company Establishment Registration Application (corporation establishment registration filing) accompanied by the certified Articles of Incorporation, name reservation certificate, subscription deposit proof, and certificates of director appointment under Article 287-12 of the Commercial Act.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: None. Korean law imposes no statutory minimum paid-up capital for a Yuhan Hoesa. The members determine the capital amount in the Articles of Incorporation, and there is no blocked escrow account requirement at the county registry. Non-resident members must route capital contributions through a Korean bank foreign currency account and observe reporting under the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act; the bank may require proof of the source of funds before the business registration certificate is issued.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLUTION OF THE FOUNDERS AND DIRECTORS OF YUHANGHOESA, ADOPTED ON 15 SEPTEMBER 2025 AT THE REGISTERED OFFICE IN SEOUL, REPUBLIC OF KOREA. WHEREAS Yuhan Hoesa, a limited liability company proposed to be incorporated under the Commercial Act of the Republic of Korea, has been formed for the business of cross-border return merchandise and reverse logistics operations, including returned goods quality grading, storage, inspection, repair intake, disposal coordination, and re-circulation; and WHEREAS the members have resolved to create a corporate body with limited liability, with no paid-in minimum capital under applicable law, and have subscribed to the capital stated in the Articles of Incorporation; and WHEREAS the Company needs to adopt a registered office, establish banking arrangements, appoint statutory officers, and authorize them to execute the licenses and permits required to lawfully operate a reverse logistics warehouse in Korea; NOW THEREFORE, IT IS RESOLVED AS FOLLOWS: 1. The subscribed capital of the Company, as specified in the Articles of Incorporation, is hereby accepted, and the contribution of each member is verified against bank deposit certificates and foreign remittance records; no share premium or in-kind asset shall be recognized unless supported by an independent valuation. 2. The Company hereby adopts the registered office at [Address in Seoul] as its statutory domicile for receipt of service, tax notices, and judicial mail, and shall hold its corporate record book and minute book at such address. 3. The following persons are appointed as officers: [Name] as Representative Executive Director, [Name] as Director and Chief Financial Officer, and [Name] as Company Secretary and Compliance Officer, each to serve until the first ordinary meeting and until earlier removal for cause under law. 4. The officers are authorized to open and maintain current accounts, foreign currency accounts, money market accounts, and payment gateway accounts with approved banks, and to sign all mandates, facility letters, and electronic banking agreements, and to become joint or sole signatories as determined by the Representative Executive Director. 5. The officers are authorized to execute any leases, warehousing agreements, transport agreements, quality control agreements, insurance policies, customs permits, fire safety declarations, environmental registrations, and all documents necessary to obtain a warehouse business registration with the competent municipal authority and a licensed customs warehouse if applicable. 6. The Director and Chief Financial Officer is directed to make all filings with the National Tax Service, preserve the company seal under dual control, and keep books recording all reverse logistics transactions, including environmental and waste manifest records. 7. These resolutions may be logged in the Corporate Record Book and presented at the next general meeting for ratification. This resolution is signed by all founders and newly appointed directors on the date first above written.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Name Search and Reservation Through Court Registry System
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Supreme Court of Korea, District Court Registration Office, access through the Saeol e-Registration Portal
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Conduct an identical and false-similarity name search against the national company name database in both Korean and English. Submit a company name reservation application containing the intended business scope for reverse logistics and returned goods quality grading, pay the online reservation fee, and obtain the Name Reservation Certificate. Where the proposed name contains geographic terms or foreign origin, request the registry to issue a preliminary admissibility note. Keep the reserved name active for the statutory reservation period; expiration of the reservation requires a new search. If any third party contests the name, either obtain a written consent in Korean from the prior registrant or submit an alternate secondary corporate name before proceeding.
required_dossiers: passport or resident identity copy of each founder
foreign non-resident address proof
proposed corporate name in Korean and English
detailed business object clause for ISIC 5229 reverse logistics
power of attorney if filed by a corporate formation agent
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the registry queries the name for confusion, correct the proposed name by filing a written alternative and consent statement within fourteen days. If the name reservation lapses during review, file a new search immediately and amend the incorporation application.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Execution, Subscription, and Deposit of Initial Capital with Foreign Exchange Clearance
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Commercial bank licensed under Korean Financial Services Commission; Foreign Exchange Information System reporting through the bank; local notary public recommended for signature certification
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: The members shall settle the exact capital amount, the method of valuation for any in-kind contribution, and the unconditional subscription obligation. Draft the Articles of Incorporation in Korean, circulate the draft among all members, and execute the document with corporate seals or electronic signatures. Certify the date and authenticity of the signatures before a notary for any foreign signatory. Open a temporary corporate account or capital subscription account and deposit each member contribution, ensuring non-resident members make remittance under the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act. Obtain a certificate of deposit, foreign remittance receipt, or bank statement describing the source. Preserve the subscription payment evidence for presentation to the court registry.
required_dossiers: executed Articles of Incorporation in Korean
Name Reservation Certificate
capital contribution payment certificate or remittance receipt
valuation report for any non-cash contribution
foreign exchange transaction report for non-resident members
photo identification of each subscribing member
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the deposit document contains a conversion mismatch between foreign currency and Korean won, instruct the bank to issue a corrected remittance advice. If a signature is defective, execute a corrected signature page before the notary and resubmit the Articles of Incorporation.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Establishment Registration with District Court Registry and Corporate Seal Acknowledgment
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: District Court Registration Office having local jurisdiction over the registered office in Seoul
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Complete the establishment registration form online or in court, attach the Articles of Incorporation, name reservation certificate, capital deposit certificate, founder identification, and the resolution appointing the Representative Executive Director and other officers. Pay the court registration tax and the education surcharge computed on the declared capital. The registrar examines the statutory legality of the objects clause, the capital subscription, and the officer appointments, and upon satisfaction enters the company into the Court Registration Ledger. After registration, obtain a certified Registration Extract and register the corporate seal specimen. Issue official Korean and English extracts for banking and commercial purposes. Legal personality commences on this registration date.
required_dossiers: establishment registration application form
Articles of Incorporation
name reservation certificate
certificate of capital deposit or remittance
founder identity documents
corporate seal specimen and seal registration form
written resolution appointing directors
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the registrar issues a supplementary correction request, amend the Articles of Incorporation and pay the statutory correction fee. If registration is refused, file an appeal or re-application with the corrected object clause and proof of contribution within the suspension period.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Business Registration, Value-Added Tax, and Payroll Setup with National Tax Service
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: National Tax Service Hometax portal and the geographically competent District Tax Office
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Within twenty-one calendar days after the court registration, file an application for business registration through Hometax, using the registered company name and the RTL warehouse and reverse logistics operations as the principal activity. Submit the court registration extract, lease contract or proof of premises, corporate seal certificate, and CEO identification. Process the application with the local tax office to receive the Business Registration Certificate and the corporate tax number. Register the company as a value-added taxpayer, obtain the e-invoice certificate, and sign up for electronic tax invoice issuance. Register for the national pension and health insurance payroll systems and confirm with the bank that payment rails for Local ACH and Airwallex are linked to the registered legal entity.
required_dossiers: business registration application through Hometax
court registration extract
lease agreement for the warehouse and office
corporate seal certificate and specimen
CEO identification copy
bank account details and payroll registration forms
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the tax office issues a supplementary demand for the lease or premises proof, upload the lease registration and a simple utility bill within three days. If the business code is misclassified, submit a correction request under the Value-Added Tax Act and resubmit in Hometax.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Warehouse, Reverse Logistics, Environmental, Fire and Occupational Licensing Permit Application
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Local municipal government (Si/Gun/Gu) industrial division; Korea Customs Service for bonded warehouse authorization; Ministry of Environment Regional Environmental Office; National Fire Agency local fire station; Ministry of Employment and Labor through Korea Occupational Safety and Health Agency
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File a warehouse business registration with the local municipal government, indicating that returned merchandise is received in closed segregated bays, undergoes quality grading, damage staging, and is either re-stocked, transferred, repaired, recycled, or disposed of through authorized channels. If imported returns are stored under customs control, submit a licensed customs warehouse application to the Korea Customs Service. Prior to lease completion, perform a site environmental screening under the Environmental Impact Assessment Act and file an environmental registration or prior environmental review where required. Submit structural load calculations, fire evacuation plans, chemical and lithium battery storage plans, noise control strategies for any sorting line, and a hazardous waste manifest program. Obtain the civil defense fire safety approval and the occupational safety health clearance before handling operations commence.
required_dossiers: lease or title deed for the warehouse
building permit and architectural floor plan
warehouse business registration application form
customs warehouse license application if bonded
environmental screening and registration forms
structural engineer structural load report
fire defense system installation plans
hazardous material inventory for returned batteries and aerosols
occupational safety health self-inspection certificate and waste disposal service agreement
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If fire clearance is denied, remediate the automatic extinguishing or evacuation deficiencies within fifteen to thirty days and request a re-inspection. If the Korea Customs Service rejects the bonded application, downgrade the operation to non-bonded status and obtain the general warehouse permit. If the environmental review requires a full EIA, retain an EIA-certified consultant and resubmit within the statutory review period.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Ministry of Land, Infrastructure and Transport for warehouse business licensing; Korea Customs Service for bonded return goods custody; local municipal government (Si/Gun/Gu) for business site and building compliance; Ministry of Environment regional office for environmental registration; National Fire Agency for fire safety; Ministry of Employment and Labor for occupational health.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Warehouse Business Registration (Warehouse Business Registration Certificate) under the Warehousing Industry Act and Trucking Transport Business Act; if necessary, a Licensed Customs Warehouse Permit under Article 179 of the Customs Act; plus a Returned Goods Re-Circulation and Quality Grading Operation Authorization issued by the local municipal trade department as an ancillary operational permit.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Ministry of Environment of the Republic of Korea together with the relevant Regional Environmental Office and local government environmental division
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Registration-Based Environmental Review (Prior Environmental Review / Small Environmental Review) for reverse logistics warehouses occupying an existing building below 5,000 square meters of floor area; Full Environmental Impact Assessment is triggered only where site preparation, construction, or land conversion exceeds 100,000 square meters in a protected watershed, greenbelt, or ecologically sensitive area. For existing facilities not creating new floorspace, an administrative environmental self-check and facility registration in lieu of full EIA is accepted.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Discharge wastewater from wash bays and spill containment areas must meet BOD less than or equal to 40 mg/L, COD less than or equal to 40 mg/L, suspended solids less than or equal to 40 mg/L, total nitrogen less than or equal to 20 mg/L, and pH 6.5 to 8.5 before municipal sewer discharge. Volatile organic compound emissions from any degreasing, marking, or repair-intake station are limited to 0.5 kg per day per emission source unless equipped with a recovery or activated carbon system. Hazardous returned items, including damaged lithium batteries, aerosols, and flammable liquids, must not exceed ten tons on-site, must be stored in segregated containers with a hazardous waste manifest, and must be transferred only to a licensed waste disposal contractor; any accidental release above reportable quantity must be notified to the regional environmental office within one hour.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire Safety Certification under the Framework Act on Fire Covers, Fire-Fighting, and Rescue; completion certificate for fire detection and suppression systems as required for warehousing and closed storage; structural load inspection certificate signed by a licensed structural engineer; occupational safety and health approval from the Korea Occupational Safety and Health Agency covering sorting lines, manual lifting posts, return-package decontamination, and battery storage; Civil Defense shelter notification and evacuation route posting for any warehouse floor area exceeding 300 square meters; and annual workplace health program submission for employees handling imported return packages, used devices, and potentially hazardous goods.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: National Tax Service (NTS) of the Republic of Korea; electronic portal HomeTax (hometax.go.kr) for national tax and VAT registration, and Korea Customs Service UNI-PASS (unipass.customs.go.kr) for customs trader registration and export/import declarations.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: Step 1: Determine whether the Yuhan Hoesa has a Korean domestic place of business (fixed place, branch, or dependent agent) or is a non-resident entity without one. Step 2: If a domestic place of business exists, file the Foreign Corporation Domestic Place of Business Registration under the Corporate Tax Act and the VAT Business Registration under the Value-Added Tax Act with the district tax office having jurisdiction over the business location via HomeTax before commencing taxable activities. Attach certified true copies of the foreign certificate of incorporation, articles of association with Korean translation, board resolution opening the Korea place of business, proof of business address, power of attorney appointing a Korean tax representative if no resident officer is present, and identification documents. Step 3: NTS will issue the unified 10-digit Business Registration Number (BRN), which is the statutory TIN used for VAT, corporate tax, withholding tax, and customs-related verification. Step 4: If the foreign entity has no domestic place of business but supplies goods or services subject to Korean VAT, the non-resident entity must file a simplified VAT registration as a foreign business operator with NTS through a tax representative and obtain a BRN for VAT. Step 5: For physical reverse logistics and returned-goods operations, register as a trader with Korea Customs Service in UNI-PASS to obtain the customs trader number required for import declarations, temporary importation, and re-export documentation. No minimum paid-in capital is required for a foreign-owned Yuhan Hoesa LLC.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: None (South Korea has no check-the-box pass-through election; a Yuhan Hoesa is taxed at entity level as a domestic corporation under the Corporate Tax Act). Eligible wholly-owned domestic corporate groups may elect consolidated corporate tax filing under the Corporate Tax Act, and hybrid mismatch treatment is mandatory under the Korean Tax Adjustment Act, not elective.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Value-Added Tax (VAT) under the Value-Added Tax Act
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: KRW 0 (no general monetary threshold; VAT registration is mandatory from the first taxable supply). A special simplified non-resident electronic/digital service supplier threshold of KRW 100,000,000 in annual Korean turnover applies, but physical reverse logistics operations performed in Korea are not within that special threshold and require registration from commencement.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: South Korea operates the HomeTax electronic tax invoice system. Every registered business operator must issue an electronic tax invoice (e-Tax Invoice) for all VAT taxable supplies, including 0% export supplies, and transmit it to NTS through HomeTax by the day following issuance. There is no transactional digital-stamping pre-approval regime; however, the e-Tax Invoice filing obligation is mandatory and NTS performs near-real-time data matching against customs declarations, import/export records, and foreign-exchange remittance records. Cash receipts are also required for consumer retail transactions where Korean cash receipt rules apply.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: A 0% VAT rate applies to exports of goods and to qualifying foreign-currency-earning services supplied to non-residents under Article 21 of the Value-Added Tax Act and Article 26 of its Enforcement Decree. For cross-border reverse logistics and returned-goods quality grading, zero-rating is available when the Yuhan Hoesa provides the service under a contract with a non-resident principal, the service is or is directly ancillary to international transport, processing, handling, or re-export of goods physically moved out of Korea, the goods are brought into Korea under a customs importation, temporary importation, bonded warehousing, or transshipment declaration and are subsequently re-exported, and the consideration is actually received in foreign currency through a Korean foreign-exchange bank or by internationally accepted remittance. Services performed wholly for domestic principals or consumed within Korea remain taxable at 10%. The exporter must issue a 0% electronic tax invoice and retain the statutory export evidence bundle.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration / Export Declaration Certificate issued by Korea Customs Service through UNI-PASS for the re-exported merchandise
Bill of Lading or Air Waybill evidencing physical exportation of the returned goods from Korea to a foreign destination
Inward Remittance Certificate / Foreign Exchange Receipt Certificate or equivalent bank remittance document issued by a Korean foreign exchange bank evidencing actual receipt of export proceeds
Import Declaration (Bill of Entry), temporary import declaration, or bonded/transshipment customs declaration for the returned goods entering Korea
Commercial invoice, packing list, and the reverse-logistics service contract/purchase order with the non-resident principal
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: NTS and Korea Customs Service cross-audit export declarations, e-tax invoices, service contracts, customs entry records, and bank remittance documents. If 0% export zero-rating is claimed without valid customs export evidence or without receipt of foreign currency within the statutory export settlement period, NTS will reverse the 0% treatment, assess 10% VAT on the full supply value, and impose statutory additional tax for underreporting or unfiled VAT, which can reach up to 40% of the unpaid tax in fraudulent concealment cases, plus statutory interest. Reassessment is generally available for 5 years, extended to 10 years for fraudulent omission, and criminal referral under the Punishment of Tax Evaders Act may result in imprisonment or fines up to 2 times the tax evaded. Any input VAT refunded on the basis of a false or unsubstantiated export claim is clawed back with statutory interest and penalties.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Bank of Korea (BOK) acting under the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act and the Foreign Investment Promotion Act, with delegated foreign exchange administration and enforcement functions exercised through licensed foreign exchange banks and the Korea Customs Service for trader declarations.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: South Korea operates a predominantly liberalised but formally regulated foreign exchange regime. Current-account transactions, including trade-related payments, service fees, and ordinary remittances, are generally freely convertible without prior approval when performed through a licensed foreign exchange bank; the bank books the transaction under a statutory purpose code and performs anti-money-laundering screening. Capital-account transactions, including inbound equity injections and outbound foreign investment, are also permitted but are subject to mandatory reporting to the Ministry of Economy and Finance or Bank of Korea, and foreign direct investment must be notified under the Foreign Investment Promotion Act to qualify for capital verification and repatriation protection. Profits and dividends may be remitted overseas upon submission of audited financial statements, tax payment certificates, board resolutions, and foreign exchange bank documentation, but the bank must verify the underlying earning capacity and absence of outstanding tax or customs issues. Surrender requirements are limited: export proceeds must be collected through licensed banks and can be retained in foreign currency accounts or converted to Korean won at the market rate; there is no forced surrender percentage. Practical hurdles include strict KYC/BO identification for offshore shareholders, documentary proof of the source of injected funds, and the need to obtain a certificate of foreign direct investment report before opening escrow or operational accounts.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Under the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act, export proceeds must be collected within 4 months from the date of export clearance unless an extension is granted by the foreign exchange bank; after collection, there is no mandatory surrender ratio, and 100% of proceeds may be retained as foreign currency deposits or converted into Korean won, with the chosen treatment reported to the relevant bank under the export receipt settlement code.

Capital Escrow Account / Basic Operational Currency Account
Capital Escrow Account / Basic Operational Currency Account

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Low viability for domestic KRW corporate treasury. Non-bank electronic money institutions and overseas fintech platforms such as Airwallex are not licensed banks under the Banking Act and cannot independently issue Korean won account numbers, receive foreign direct investment capital, or provide statutory FX purpose-code reporting to the Bank of Korea. They may serve only as supplementary payment collection services outside the regulated capital-account framework; all inbound capital injections, export proceeds, and repatriation flows must be housed in a tier-1 Korean commercial bank to satisfy regulatory capital verification.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: In-person opening is generally mandatory for the statutory director or a named corporate signatory at the branch; remote consular proxy opening is not accepted by most tier-1 Korean banks for foreign-owned newly formed KR LLC entities. The authorised officer must bring the company seal or power of attorney, certificate of incorporation, register of directors, shareholder identification, and pass a compliance interview; the bank may also request a physical visit to the registered office if lease and operation documents show material inconsistency.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: UBO opacity: Korean LLC shareholders include a non-resident holding company with no clear natural-person ownership chain
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Certified corporate registry abstract, complete shareholder ledger, organisational chart, passport copies of ultimate natural-person shareholders, UBO declaration, and a notarised source-of-wealth statement for each material owner.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Injected capital amount not aligned with the stated reverse-logistics business model, raising layering and trade-sanction red flags
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Detailed business plan, executed client contracts for return-merchandise fulfilment and quality grading, warehouse lease contract, historical cash-flow projections, pro-forma invoices, and bank statements from the remitting account showing clean payment rationale.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Trade counterparties located in sanctioned or FATF-blacklisted jurisdictions in the reverse-logistics supply chain
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Full counterparty due-diligence file including certificates of incorporation, beneficial-owner declarations, sanctions screening results, export/import licences, transport contracts, and a written compliance opinion confirming no sanctioned parties or prohibited goods are involved.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Mismatch between registered business purpose, tax registration, and physical operation site triggering false-entity suspicion
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Business registration certificate, VAT tax registration, office lease agreement, utility invoices, employee payroll records, on-site photographs, corporate mobile number, and a board resolution confirming the actual operation address.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Inbound equity capital for the Korean LLC must be reported as foreign direct investment under the Foreign Investment Promotion Act. The overseas shareholder initiates a SWIFT MT103 for the capital amount to the Korean LLC's KRW or foreign-currency account at a licensed foreign exchange bank, quoting the statutory foreign-exchange purpose code for equity investment and the corporate name. The Korean receiving bank verifies the deposit, files the FDI report with the Korea Trade-Investment Promotion Agency or the Ministry of Trade, Industry and Energy, and performs capital verification by comparing the remittance, the authorised share capital stated in the articles of incorporation, the investor shareholder list, and the certificate of foreign-investment report. Only after capital verification may the escrow balance be released for operational funding.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Outbound payments for returned-merchandise settlement, logistics services, and quality-grading fees are executed through SWIFT MT103 wire transfers, commercial letters of credit, or documentary collections depending on transaction size and trade terms. Domestic KRW payments use the Korean interbank wire system for same-day clearing; cross-border USD or EUR transactions require a licensed FX bank to debit the KRW or foreign-currency account, allocate a valid trade/current-account purpose code, and retain invoices, packing lists, logistics waybills, and tax invoices in the bank's compliance file.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Onshore deliverable KRW/USD forward contracts with licensed domestic banks for permitted current-account and FDI-related underlying exposures
Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) for non-resident counterparties hedging KRW trade receivables without physical settlement
Cross-currency swaps limited to actual commercial or investment exposures with fixed notional not exceeding projected trade cash flows
Outright FX forwards prohibited for speculative or uncovered positions under the Korean prudential regulations

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Corporate income tax final return (including 10% local corporate income tax surcharge) and interim prepayment
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: National Tax Service of South Korea via HomeTax electronic filing system (local surcharge collected through NTS and allocated to the relevant local government)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Final return and payment by March 31 following the December 31 fiscal year-end; interim prepayment by August 31; non-calendar fiscal year-end: final return within 3 months and interim payment within 6 months after fiscal year-end
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Non-filing penalty of 20% of the corrected tax payable, under-reporting penalty of 10% of the omitted tax, statutory late-payment interest (currently 3.4% per annum daily accrual), plus a 0.3% delinquency collection charge after the NTS demand date; prolonged non-compliance enables NTS asset seizure, business registration cancellation and a court application for judicial dissolution. Korean law has no automatic common-law administrative strike-off, but terminal non-filing is treated as de facto closure.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Value-added tax returns for corporate taxpayers (preliminary and final returns)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: National Tax Service of South Korea via HomeTax
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Four filing and payment events per calendar year: January 25 for October-December VAT, April 25 for January-March preliminary VAT, July 25 for April-June final VAT, and October 25 for July-September preliminary VAT
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Penalty additions under the VAT Act: 10% of unpaid VAT for under-declaration, 20% for non-filing, 0.5% of supply value for missing or false tax invoices, plus 3.4% per annum late-payment interest; repeated failure to file can result in business registration cancellation and summary collection enforcement by the NTS.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Monthly payroll withholding tax remittance and return (resident employment income, pension and social insurance contributions where applicable)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: National Tax Service of South Korea via HomeTax
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: By the 10th day of the month following the month in which salaries and wages were paid
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to withhold or remit triggers a 10% withholding addition on the unremitted amount, late-payment interest, personal assessment against the responsible withholding agent/director, and NTS seizure of company bank accounts and receivables.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual foreign-invested enterprise status report (applicable only if the Yuhan Hoesa has registered foreign investment)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Ministry of Trade, Industry and Energy (MOTIE) through KOTRA / Invest Korea one-stop service
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: By March 31 following the end of the prior calendar year for calendar-year enterprises; within 30 days after any change in foreign investment registration matters, including share transfers
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Administrative fine up to KRW 1,000,000 for late or omitted filing under the Foreign Investment Promotion Act; loss of or suspension of foreign-investment tax benefits and possible cancellation of the foreign investment registration; no direct corporate strike-off effect.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual general meeting of members and formal approval of financial statements and profit appropriation
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Corporate minute book maintained at the registered office; no external filing required for a private Yuhan Hoesa unless audited financial statements must be attached to tax or FSS disclosures
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 3 months after fiscal year-end, i.e. by March 31 for a December 31 year-end
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: No direct government fine for a private LLC, but directors are jointly and severally liable to the company and creditors for losses caused by failure to convene; financial statements without member approval are treated as defective for NTS audit purposes and may trigger tax penalties.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: External audit report and audited annual financial statements (triggered only when the statutory audit threshold is met)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Financial Supervisory Service (FSS) electronic disclosure system DART and, where applicable, the commercial registration court and NTS attachment to corporate tax return
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Auditor's report and audited financial statements must be finalized no later than March 31 following a December 31 fiscal year-end (within 3 months of the general meeting approval); auditor appointment changes must be reported to FSS within 2 weeks
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Under the Act on External Audit and Accounting, failure to undergo a statutory audit or file the audit report may result in FSS designation of an auditor at company expense, administrative fines up to KRW 30,000,000, criminal prosecution for use of false or missing audited statements, and NTS rejection or adjustment of the corporate tax return.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Article 2 of the Act on External Audit and Accounting (formerly the Act on External Audit of Stock Companies) makes an independent CPA audit compulsory for a Yuhan Hoesa LLC if total assets at the end of the immediately preceding fiscal year equal or exceed KRW 10,000,000,000 (approximately USD 7.5 million at KRW 1,330/USD); for a joint-stock company the threshold is KRW 12,000,000,000 (approximately USD 9.0 million). Korean external audit law uses an asset-based balance-sheet trigger; there is no turnover or employee-headcount test. Audit is also compulsory irrespective of asset size if the company issues debt securities to the public, is designated as a public-interest company under Article 5, is a large consolidated subsidiary of a listed group, or is otherwise selected for external audit by the Financial Supervisory Service. Below the threshold, an LLC may voluntarily prepare CPA-reviewed or compiled financial statements, but no statutory opinion is required.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Korean International Financial Reporting Standards (K-IFRS) apply to companies that must adopt K-IFRS (listed entities, financial institutions and public-interest entities); a private non-listed Yuhan Hoesa may use Korean GAAP (K-GAAP) for non-listed entities, which is aligned with IFRS for SMEs. Financial statements must be prepared in Korean won and in the Korean language, with an independent auditor's report issued under K-IFRS or K-GAAP as applicable. Accounting standards are issued by the Korea Accounting Standards Board (KASB).

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: South Korea does not currently require a separate annual UBO return for a private Yuhan Hoesa LLC. The mandatory protocol is: (1) maintain an accurate register of members at the registered office at all times; (2) record any transfer of membership interest, pledge or change of ownership in the register promptly, because a transfer is not effective against third parties until entered in the register; (3) if the LLC is a foreign-invested enterprise, report any change in foreign shareholding or foreign investment registration to MOTIE/KOTRA within 30 days; (4) file the annual foreign-invested enterprise status report by March 31 identifying major foreign shareholders; and (5) perform an annual internal compliance sign-off in Q1 reconciling the register of members with bank account ownership, tax filings, dividend records and any foreign investment registration. The 30-day post-event reporting window is the only statutory UBO-affecting deadline under the Foreign Investment Promotion Act.

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 700 - 1,500 per annum for a standard Seoul registered office address, registered agent and compliance desk in South Korea
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 0 for an LLC below the mandatory audit threshold; if statutory or voluntarily required, generally USD 5,000 - 18,000 per annum for a small or medium Korean LLC

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 24% national headline rate plus 10% local income tax surtax, producing a 26.4% aggregate top effective corporate tax rate for taxable income exceeding KRW 300 billion
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: General statutory rates are 9% for income up to KRW 200 million, 19% from KRW 200 million to KRW 20 billion, 21% from KRW 20 billion to KRW 300 billion, and 24% above KRW 300 billion; SMBs benefit from lower brackets and credits; preferential foreign-investment tax holidays and 50%-100% deductions are available for qualified FDI projects in economic free zones under the Restriction of Special Taxation Act; R&D spending credits range from 25% to 50% and a patent/offshore IP box-style exemption is available for qualifying IP-derived income; aggregate local income tax surcharge is 10% of the national corporate tax due.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Corporate Tax Return (Korean Form No. 24, Corporate Tax Base and Tax Amount Calculation Statement) and all supplementary schedules; filed through the National Tax Service HomeTax electronic filing portal
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Within 3 months from the end of each fiscal year, or by March 31 for calendar-year taxpayers; a limited extension is available for audited foreign-parent consolidated financial statements, but the extension must be applied for and cannot exceed one month on a non-notice basis

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Report gross business income from reverse-logistics services, returned-merchandise grading fees, storage fees, and all deductible expenses including warehouse rent, freight, labor, insurance, and impairment losses on returned inventory.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident shareholders must ensure all income attributable to a Korean permanent establishment is included; offshore quality-grading or dispatch activities that are treaty-protected must not create a PE and must be footnoted with supporting substance evidence such as local employees, premises, and risk-taking functions.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Book net income before tax after reconciliation of Korean-form K-IFRS financial statements with tax-adjusted accounts.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: For a foreign-owned Korean LLC, disallowed expenses such as excessive group management fees, royalties lacking economic substance, and interest exceeding the thin-capitalization safe harbour must be adjusted upward on this line.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Taxable income after statutory adjustments, net operating loss deductions, tax credit carryovers, and special deductions for foreign investments or SME preferential rates.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Any NOL carryforward is available only to a timely-filed tax return and only for 10 years from the loss year; a foreign-controlled Korean company cannot carry losses against income if it has been reclassified as a permanent establishment of the foreign parent under a sham-entity determination.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Declaration of domestic-source income paid to non-residents and withholding tax withheld on outbound dividends, interest, royalties, and cross-border service fees.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Attach a schedule identifying each non-resident recipient, the beneficial owner, the TRC reference, and the treaty article relied on; no reduced treaty rate may be reflected without a fully executed treaty relief application and substantiated economic substance.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Computation of final corporate tax after foreign tax credits, interim tax prepayments, construction reserves, and other credits, with the final balance payable or refundable.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Dividends declared to the foreign parent must be traced to accumulated post-tax retained earnings; if the parent claims a 5% or 10% treaty dividend rate, the 25% shareholding test, LOB clause, and Tax Residency Certificate must be satisfied, otherwise the full statutory 22% must be withheld.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Report surcharges for late filing, underreporting, false returns, and failure to attach mandatory transfer pricing documentation or international transaction schedules.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Cross-border filings must be complete before the statutory deadline; a late or inaccurate schedule may trigger a 20% unfaithful-return penalty plus 0.022% daily interest on the tax underpaid, and may further expose the foreign group to NTS transfer pricing reassessment.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late-filing surcharge: 20% of the unpaid corporate tax; underpayment daily interest: 0.022% per day from the due date until paid; unfaithful return penalty: 10% of the underreported amount; fraudulent return or false-invoice penalty: 40% of the underreported amount; criminal prosecution under the Punishment of Tax Evaders Act carries imprisonment of up to 5 years or a fine of up to 3 times the evaded tax, with aggravated penalties for amounts exceeding KRW 5 billion.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 22% aggregate statutory withholding on outbound Korean-source dividends paid to non-resident shareholders, composed of 20% corporate/individual income tax and 2% local income tax surcharge; bilateral treaty relief commonly reduces the rate to 5% where the parent company owns at least 25% of the voting shares and meets the Limitation on Benefits clause, and to 15% in other shareholding cases
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: To claim DTA relief, the non-resident shareholder must: (1) receive a Tax Residency Certificate (TRC) from its own competent tax authority; (2) submit through HomeTax the standard Korean application for exemption from or reduction of withholdings to the NTS before or at the time of the payment, together with a beneficial ownership declaration; (3) prove the parent is the true owner of the dividend, interest, or royalty income and is not a conduit, using accounts, board resolutions, substance evidence, and corporate charters; (4) if the statutory 22% was already withheld, file a refund claim with the NTS within the applicable five-year statute of limitations, attaching the same TRC, treaty-relief form, and a written memorandum of law; and (5) respond to any NTS challenge within 60 days or risk deemed rejection and reassessment at the domestic rate plus interest.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Statutory withholding on outbound royalties and intercompany interest is also 22% aggregate (20% plus 2% local surcharge); tax treaties often reduce interest to 0-10% and royalties to 5-10%, but only when the recipient is the beneficial owner, the payments are at arm's length, and the recipient has sufficient underlying economic activity to satisfy the treaty's beneficial ownership and anti-conduit requirements.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: KRW 10 billion aggregate cross-border related-party transaction amount for a fiscal year, which triggers mandatory Local File and Master File preparation and submission to the NTS within 45 days of the corporate tax return deadline; below the threshold, contemporaneous TP documentation must still be prepared because the NTS can demand it and assess penalties for failure to produce records within 60 days
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Although Korea does not have a standalone Economic Substance Regulations regime in the Gulf-country format, Korean tax law applies the substance-over-form doctrine through Article 14 of the Framework Act on National Taxes, the Korea International Tax Adjustment Act, and OECD BEPS Action 6 treaty-abuse protections. A Korean reverse-logistics company must demonstrate a real Core Income-Generating Activity inside Korea, including physical warehouse facilities, local managers, operational risk, inventory control decisions, grading teams, and customer interface; a shell entity with no employees and no commercial decision-making is subject to recharacterization, denial of treaty benefits, withholding reassessment, transfer pricing adjustments, and criminal tax-evasion exposure.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Deliberately omitting Korean-source revenue from reverse-logistics and returned-goods grading services, issuing false invoices to understate taxable income, or disguising dividend distributions as offshore management fees or royalty payments to the foreign parent to avoid Korean withholding tax.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Punishment of Tax Evaders Act Article 3; imprisonment for up to 5 years or a fine of not more than 3 times the evaded tax; additionally, a fraudulent-return penalty of 40% of the underreported tax plus daily interest of 0.022%; evasion above KRW 5 billion triggers aggravated imprisonment of 5 to 10 years and confiscation of tax benefits.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: The corporate veil is pierced when the managing director and foreign beneficial owners jointly engineer the fraudulent scheme; directors are jointly and severally liable for the corporate tax, surcharges, and criminal fines from their personal assets; the NTS may impose a travel ban/blacklisting, seize bank accounts and real estate, and the responsible director and beneficial owner face imprisonment in Korea with possible Interpol red-notice coordination.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Shell Company / Treaty Abuse / Lack of Economic Substance
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Operating the Korean entity as a paper holding or conduit company with no employees, no physical warehouse, no operational risk, and no local decision-making; all returned-merchandise grading and logistics functions are performed by the foreign parent, while the Korean entity records an artificially low margin and remits residual profits as tax-exempt or treaty-reduced payments.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: NTS denial under the substance-over-form doctrine in Article 14 of the Framework Act on National Taxes, the Korea International Tax Adjustment Act, and OECD BEPS Action 6; the tax authority can reassess a deemed PE, impute arm's-length income, deny treaty relief on dividends and royalties, and impose a 40% unjustified-benefit penalty plus 0.022% daily interest; where sham transactions are proven, prosecution under the Punishment of Tax Evaders Act follows.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and shareholders who intentionally used the Korean entity as a sham bear personal civil liability for the full reassessed taxes and penalties; Korean courts may pierce the veil where the entity is undercapitalized and lacks a separate identity; foreign owners may be personally blacklisted, have Korean assets restrained, and be subject to extradition or red-notice procedures, with imprisonment imposed on the local representative and, in egregious cases, on the foreign owner as co-principal.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: AML / Beneficial Ownership Filing / Undisclosed International Fund Movements
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Failing to file beneficial ownership information of the ultimate foreign LLC parent, failing to declare wire transfers and cash settlement flows exceeding KRW 30 million, or using the Korean entity's bank account for undisclosed remittances linked to returned-merchandise transactions with foreign counterparties.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Act on Reporting and Use of Certain Financial Transaction Information Article 33: imprisonment up to 5 years or a fine up to KRW 50 million for AML reporting violations; Foreign Exchange Transactions Act penalties up to 5 years or KRW 100 million for unreported capital transactions; combined NTS and customs review may add 20% undisclosed-income tax and 40% dishonest-return penalties.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors, the compliance officer, and the ultimate beneficial owner are personally exposed to criminal prosecution as principal wrongdoers; the corporate veil does not block personal asset forfeiture, bank-account freezing, travel bans, or blacklisting by the Korean Financial Intelligence Unit and Korea Customs; management may face imprisonment and each responsible director may be jointly liable for all unpaid taxes, penalties, and the cost of any asset-tracing investigation.
